newsitem.title: RUSSIA: LUKoil has deal for 10 pct of Chevron Tengiz stake.
newsitem.headline: LUKoil has deal for 10 pct of Chevron Tengiz stake.

text.p: Russia's NK LUKoil said in a statement on Thursday that it had completed talks with Chevron Corp to acquire 10 percent of the U.S. oil major's stake in the $20 billion Tengiz oil project in Kazakhstan.

"Today, January 16, 1997, Russian oil company LUKoil and American oil corporation Chevron completed talks on the terms under which Chevron will give up 10 percent of its stake in the TengizChevroil partnership," it said.
Chevron Corp owns 50 percent in TengizChevroil (TCO), while fellow U.S. oil major Mobil Corp and the Kazakh government each own 25 percent.
LUKoil's purchase from Chevron of a 10 percent stake would give it a five percent share overall in the joint venture.

The statement quoted LUKoil Vice-President Dzevhan Cheloyants as saying Russia's biggest oil company and Chevron had reached mutual understanding on all basic conditions of the agreement. It gave no further information.
LUKoil President Vagit Alekperov said on Wednesday that LUKoil expected to conclude the terms of the purchase by early February.
Tengiz, in western Kazakhstan, has estimated crude oil reserves of six to nine billion barrels.
Output is already at around 160,000 barrels per day and is expected to rise to 700,000 bpd by 2010.
